items.title: Proposed new Summarization option to identify "Additional Licenses"
items.body:
Please consider a new Summarization option to identify and collect "Additional licenses"  in license-expression format:

Suggested definition of the new field: 

Identifies licenses detected in the lower level files of a software package that are not the same as the license(s) declared as primary for a package (or software project). Note that these licenses are often assigned to files intended for testing or reference that are not necessarily part of the code that is actually built and deployed.

Benefits: 
Most open source projects have a declared primary license, but the very nature of open source continues to create complex releases of projects that have increasingly great numbers of different licenses in various files pulled in from other projects.  These are generally compatible (always the best objective) but it is useful to show them separately for review and documentation purposes.

items.title: considering "License: BSD" as meaning bsd-new should include some notion of uncertainty
items.body:
The test src/licensedcode/data/rules/bsd-new_89.yml is categorized as bsd-new, but contains only this:
> License: BSD

I disagree that "BSD" equals "BSD-3-Clause" - sure, that is the "more original among the Free flavors" and also the more common among all of them.  But neither is a reason for reliable disambiguation.

I think the most sensible is to classify this as "any of the BSD licenses, but not possible to tell which".
In licensecheck that is labeled as "BSD~unspecified".

Consequently, I think test src/licensedcode/data/rules/bsd-new_100.RULE should be categorized as "BSD-3-Clause and/or BSD~unspecified" (not as "BSD-3-Clause" because even though the subsequent text is unambiguous, is it not clear if or how the two statements correlate (there is no implicit "one means same as the other" nor is there an "choose one or the other" or "you must apply both one and the other")

items.body:
Hi

I am new to Scancode and I did not manage to add a new license or rule. I have installed Scancode (version 31.2.4) on a windows 10 machine, via Git Bash by cloning the github project. I ran the tool on some test files and it seems to be working fine, however I wanted add a new license and a new rule for it.

My files: [zz-test.zip](https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/files/11499750/zz-test.zip)
I have created zz-test.LICENSE and 4 .RULE files (zz-test.RULE and zz-test_1 to 3). I created the license file here: scancode-toolkit\src\licensedcode\data\licenses and the rule files here: scancode-toolkit\src\licensedcode\data\rules

I have attached the files. After creating the file I ran "scancode --reindex-licenses" and then I ran "scancode -clpeui --html test_files_results.html test_files". The "test_files" directory contains only one file: mihai_file.h that contains:
/*
 *  Copyright Mihai C.
 *
 *  This is my custom test license.
 *  Use for testing purposes only!
 */

#ifndef _SAMPLE_DRV_H_
#define _SAMPLE_DRV_H_

I used to read the documentation from https://scancode-toolkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/how-to-guides/add_new_license_detection_rule.html but since yesterday I also read the https://scancode-toolkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to-guides/add_new_license_detection_rule.html

Sadly, I still cannot figure what I am doing wrong or why the tool does not detect my test license.

items.title: Externalize licenses rules and tests in new repo: collaboration with Debian
items.body:
I chatted with Debian developers: @jonassmedegaard in particular and  we agreed to start some collaboration. 

The data set of licenses and licenses tests available in scancode is rather meaty (and possibly quite unique and valuable of its own).

The idea would be to externalize and promote the licenses, rules and test data to their own repository  such that the Debian maintainers and anyone else can use building license detection tools can reuse these possibly to refine other tools. And we can also all collaborate more easily to make this data better and richer for everyone.

The project would likely live at https://alioth.debian.org/projects/licenses/ and may be mirrored to Github for convenience (for scancode users/contributors)

Others have expressed some interest or a positive feedback on the idea:
 @marga-debian  @maxyz  @zacchiro @olasd @carandraug @dod38fr

items.title: Add new tests for license detection using an older SPDX dataset
items.body:
I got a report that the license detection on this dataset https://github.com/spdx/license-list/tree/v1.19 was a tad surprising because there were some false positive.

This is an older SPDX licenses list and it has a few problems leading to these from a quick look:
- some text contain extra commentary such as : `<insert GPLv2 full text here>` which would lead to a detection
- some text have mojibake https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojibake e.g damaged unicode/utf characters that triggers a detection which is not with a 100% score
- it contains some spreadsheets of the whole licenses list and scancode does digs in these alright even if they are binaries leading to many extra detections...

That said, I still want to add these as a test and eventually ensure with appropriate rules that we have 100% detection with 100% score on this dataset.

items.title: Add new and improved license detection rules
Add new plugin to detect if a file is all licenses #1366
items.body:
The new command line option is "--is-license-text"
It requires the --license --info --license-text and --license-diag
options. If a file contains 80% or more of license text characters
based on what was detected, then the attribute is_license_text i set
as true for that file.

Signed-off-by: Philippe Ombredanne <pombredanne@nexb.com>
